This guide is for packages that read ALTREP character vectors, register an
ALTREP string class, or build `charvec` output.

`charport::Reader` exposes low-level byte views and their lifetime guarantees.
Encoding policy remains with the consumer.

The guide is organized around three use cases:

| Section | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [Using `Reader`](#universal-reader) | Read registered ALTREP strings through one C++ interface. |
| [Registering an ALTREP class](#altrep-registration) | Make an ALTREP string class readable by other packages through `charport`. |
| [Using `charvec` directly](#charvec-direct) | Build `charvec` output directly with serial or multithreaded builders. |

All three use cases start the same way: link to `charport`, include the umbrella
header, and check the ABI once when your package loads.

## Linking to `charport` {#linking-to-charport}

Use the C++ interface in `charport.h`.

In `DESCRIPTION`, declare both the runtime dependency and the header dependency:

```text
Imports:
    charport
LinkingTo:
    charport
```

In `NAMESPACE`, load your package's native code and import `charport` so its
runtime entry points are available:

### Namespace setup {.tabset}

#### NAMESPACE

```text
useDynLib(yourpkg, .registration = TRUE)
import(charport)
```

#### roxygen2

```r
#' @useDynLib yourpkg, .registration = TRUE
#' @import charport
"_PACKAGE"
```

### ABI check hook {.tabset}

`charport::check_abi()` verifies that the installed package matches the headers
used to compile the consumer. Call it once from native initialization, using a
manual, Rcpp, or cpp11 hook. An `.onLoad` wrapper is also possible.

#### Rcpp init

```cpp
#include "charport.h"

// [[Rcpp::init]]
void init_yourpkg(DllInfo * dll) {
  charport::check_abi();
  (void)dll;
}
```

#### cpp11 init

```cpp
#include "charport.h"

[[cpp11::init]]
void init_yourpkg(DllInfo * dll) {
  charport::check_abi();
  (void)dll;
}
```

#### Manual init

```cpp
#include "charport.h"

extern "C" void R_init_yourpkg(DllInfo * dll) {
  R_registerRoutines(dll, NULL, call_entries, NULL, NULL);
  R_useDynamicSymbols(dll, FALSE);
  charport::check_abi();
  R_forceSymbols(dll, TRUE);
}
```

#### Manual `.onLoad`

```cpp
#include "charport.h"

extern "C" SEXP C_check_charport_abi(void) {
  charport::check_abi();
  return R_NilValue;
}
```

Register `C_check_charport_abi` in the package's `.Call` table, then add:

```r
.onLoad <- function(libname, pkgname) {
  .Call(C_check_charport_abi)
}
```

The current ABI version is `CHARPORT_ABI_VERSION=1`. Any layout or contract
break bumps this value. `check_abi()` compares the version compiled into
`yourpkg` with the installed `charport` version and throws if they differ.

## Using `Reader` {#universal-reader}

`charport::Reader` reads string data from a registered ALTREP class or an
ordinary R character vector. Construct it from a character vector, then access
elements by iteration or index.

```cpp
using namespace charport;
Reader r(robj);
for(StrView s : r) {
  // ...
}

for(R_xlen_t i=0; i<r.size(); ++i) {
  StrView s = r[i];
  if(!s.is_na()) {
    // s.ptr, s.len, s.enc
  }
}
```

For a registered ALTREP class, `Reader` gives you non-materializing views. For a plain vector, a materialized ALTREP vector or an ALTREP vector that is not registered, `Reader` falls back to ordinary access via `STRING_PTR_RO`.

### Reader kind

`Reader::kind()` reports how the current `Reader` was resolved. It describes the read path chosen when
the `Reader` was constructed.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `charport::ReaderKind::PLAIN` | Ordinary non-ALTREP character vector. |
| `charport::ReaderKind::MATERIALIZED_ALTREP` | ALTREP character vector whose ordinary string storage is already available. |
| `charport::ReaderKind::REGISTERED_ALTREP` | ALTREP character vector served by a `charport`-registered class. |
| `charport::ReaderKind::FALLBACK_ALTREP` | ALTREP character vector not served directly; resolving the `Reader` falls back to ordinary R string access. |

`Reader::view_persistence()` and `Reader::thread_safe_access()` report the two
primitive reader guarantees. `Reader::reentrant()` is a convenience check that
returns true only when both guarantees are true.

### `StrView`

`StrView` is the element type returned by `Reader`. It is a non-owning view of
bytes owned by the character vector.

Each `StrView` contains:

1. `ptr`, a pointer to the string data
2. `len`, the length of the string in bytes
3. `enc`, the encoding mark for those bytes

`ptr` is not guaranteed to be null-terminated; use `len` for its byte length.

`enc` is an extended enum similar to, but not identical to, base R's
`cetype_t`. The following values are defined:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `charport_enc::CE_NATIVE` | Native encoding based on machine locale. |
| `charport_enc::CE_UTF8` | UTF-8. |
| `charport_enc::CE_LATIN1` | Latin-1. |
| `charport_enc::CE_BYTES` | Bytes encoding. |
| `charport_enc::CE_ASCII_OR_UTF8` | ASCII/UTF-8-compatible bytes. |
| `charport_enc::CE_ASCII` | ASCII bytes, equivalent to `Rf_charIsASCII(x)`. |
| `charport_enc::CE_NA` | Missing string. `ptr` is `NULL` and `len` is zero. |

These fields carry the byte data and encoding information represented by a base
R `CHARSXP`.

### Reader lifetime and multithreading

In Rust terms, a `Reader` acts like a strict borrow. It is a temporary view of
the vector's current string storage, valid only while that storage remains
protected and unmodified.

R accessors on the original vector (`STRING_ELT()`, `STRING_PTR_RO()`, `DATAPTR_RO()`, etc.) can invalidate the `Reader`.

When `view_persistence()` is true, `StrView` pointers returned from the
`Reader` remain valid after later `Reader` access, until the active borrow ends.
This allows code to collect views on the main thread and process on worker threads.

When `thread_safe_access()` is true, `Reader` access itself may happen off the
main thread and concurrently. `reentrant()` returns true only when both
`view_persistence()` and `thread_safe_access()` are true.

The fallback `Reader` path over `CHARSXP`s has persistent views but is
main-thread-only for access. It uses R's string objects and accessors.

## Registering an ALTREP class {#altrep-registration}

A package registers its ALTREP class after creating it. Registration can happen
directly in native package initialization, or from `.onLoad()` via a small
native routine.

### Registration location {.tabset}

Native package initialization is the usual registration point. An `.onLoad`
wrapper can call the same native registration routine.

#### Init hook registration example
```cpp
static R_altrep_class_t your_altrep;

extern "C" void R_init_yourpkg(DllInfo * dll) {
  // Other init hook operations
  // ...
  your_altrep = R_make_altstring_class("yourclass", "yourpkg", dll);
  charport::check_abi();
  charport::register_altrep(your_altrep, init_fn, get_fn, true, true);
}

extern "C" void R_unload_yourpkg(DllInfo * dll) {
  charport::unregister_altrep(your_altrep);
  (void)dll;
}
```
Rcpp and cpp11 initialization hooks can perform the same registration.

#### .onLoad hook registration example

```cpp
extern "C" SEXP C_register_yourpkg_altrep(void) {
  charport::check_abi();
  charport::register_altrep(your_altrep, init_fn, get_fn, true, true);
  return R_NilValue;
}

extern "C" SEXP C_unregister_yourpkg_altrep(void) {
  charport::unregister_altrep(your_altrep);
  return R_NilValue;
}
```

```r
.onLoad <- function(libname, pkgname) {
  .Call(C_register_yourpkg_altrep)
}

.onUnload <- function(libpath) {
  .Call(C_unregister_yourpkg_altrep)
}
```

The registration function has the following signature:

```cpp
void charport::register_altrep(
  R_altrep_class_t cls,
  charport_init_fn init,
  charport_get_strview_fn get_strview,
  bool view_persistence,
  bool thread_safe_access
);
```

If `your_altrep` is already registered, `register_altrep()` throws an error.
Duplicate registration usually means the package registered from more than one
load hook or failed to unregister before reload.

`init_fn(SEXP x)` returns the per-vector state that `get_fn()` needs. The state
is borrowed; `charport` never frees it. A class implementation that needs a lazy
index or cache should build it in `init` on the main R thread and attach it to
the ALTREP object so R owns the lifetime. Returning `NULL` means this vector
cannot be served zero-copy, so `charport` falls back to the direct path.

`get_fn(void * state, R_xlen_t i)` returns the view for element `i`. It receives
only class-specific state and the index; it must not need the original `SEXP`.

### Error and unwind rules

No C++ exception may cross the `charport` C ABI or an R `.Call` boundary.

Registered `init(SEXP)` runs on the main R thread and may report failure with
`Rf_error()`. Registered `get(state, i)` should be total for valid `i`; it must
not call the R API and must not throw. If a C++ implementation can fail,
translate that failure before crossing the ABI boundary or make it impossible by
construction.

Consumer-side C++ code that catches exceptions and reports R errors should let
the C++ exception unwind before calling `Rf_error()`. Calling `Rf_error()` from
inside a catch block can bypass C++ cleanup in that catch scope.

Long-running materialization loops in `charport` do not check user interrupts.
Interrupting midway through native store release or ALTREP materialization would
be harder to reason about than completing the operation.

## Using `charvec` directly {#charvec-direct}

Use `charport::charvec::Builder` for serial construction:

```cpp
charport::charvec::Builder b(n);
b.set(i, ptr, len, charport_enc::CE_UTF8);
SEXP out = b.to_charvec();
```

Use `reserve()` when the output bytes can be written directly into the store:

```cpp
char * dst = b.reserve(i, len, charport_enc::CE_UTF8);
std::memcpy(dst, src, len);
```

Use `charport::charvec::BuilderMT` for parallel construction. The builder owns a
fixed set of shards. Each worker must use a distinct shard index and write a
disjoint element range. Worker calls to `set()` and `reserve()` do not touch the
R API. `to_charvec()` runs on the main R thread after all workers have joined.

Both builders are single-shot after `to_charvec()` or `release_store()`. Call
`reset()` before reuse. Unwritten elements remain `NA`.

The builders throw C++ exceptions for programming errors such as out-of-range
indices, invalid shard indices, negative lengths, and strings larger than R's
single-string size limit. Catch those exceptions before returning to R.

## `charvec` store notes

`charvec` stores one fixed record array plus a chain of owned payload blocks.
Each record is exactly the ABI view type, so the registered class accessor can
return `records[i]`.

The reference class for `charvec` is registered automatically when `charport`
loads, so downstream consumers can read `charvec` objects through `Reader`
without any extra setup. Registering the same ALTREP class again is an error.

During construction, each writer owns a private shard with a bump-allocated
slice chain. Finishing a builder splices shard chains into the store without
copying payload. This is the reason sharded construction can avoid locking when
element ranges are disjoint.

Post-construction mutation may reuse an element's current bytes when the new
string fits; a grow allocates a fresh slice and leaves old bytes unreferenced
until manual compaction. Compaction rewrites live payload into fresh slices and
moves pointers, so it must not happen during an active `Reader` borrow.

## Serialization

`charvec` serialized state currently uses:

1. A magic/version prefix.
2. A one-byte endian flag.
3. Native-endian integer fields.
4. Encoding bytes and payload bytes.

On read, `charport` checks the flag and byte-swaps integer fields only when the
serialized state came from a machine with the opposite endianness. This keeps
the common path simple. Big-endian hardware is not available in the normal test
matrix, so tests include a synthetic opposite-endian serialized state; real
big-endian coverage should be added if a runner becomes available.

The serialized format is not frozen until the first CRAN release.

## Consumer runtime checklist

1. Call `charport::check_abi()` at load time.
2. Construct `Reader` objects on the main R thread.
3. Respect the borrow rule: no R access to the source vector or aliases during
   active reads.
4. Call `Reader` access from worker threads only when `r.thread_safe_access()` is true.
5. Catch C++ exceptions before returning to R.

## Class checklist

1. Register in `R_init_<pkg>()` or `.onLoad` after ALTREP class creation.
2. Unregister in `.onUnload`.
3. Keep class-specific state alive through R-owned ALTREP data.
4. Return `NULL` from `init` when a vector can no longer be served zero-copy.
5. Make `get` R-free, exception-free, and total for valid indices.
6. Set `view_persistence = true` only when returned views remain valid until the borrow ends.
7. Set `thread_safe_access = true` only when concurrent calls are actually safe.

## Testing pattern

`charport` tests downstream-style consumers by compiling small DSOs under
`tests/` against the installed headers. One consumer exercises `Reader` and
the builders through `R_GetCCallable`; another uses real `std::thread` workers
without requiring thread flags in the `charport` package itself. Packages that
integrate with `charport` should use the same pattern for their own compiled
interop tests.
